correctness.rationale: An arbitrary symmetric subset at c is contained in the reflected intersection M(c), itself symmetric and convex. Disk cross-section intersections strictly force every optimal center onto the cut axis. The exact axial section integral excludes negative centers and reduces to two differentiable branches. The ratio f(2s-a)/f(s) is strictly decreasing on the rising branch and has a unique crossing with 1/2 above the exact critical cut; below, s=0 is the unique maximizer. Algebra gives the stated root and all endpoint cases. The n=3 hemisphere ratio and thin-cap limit are explicitly derived from these integrals. A self-contained standard-library program passed 16566 axial and 420 nonaxial numerical tests as nonexhaustive corroboration.
